page: Amazon Web Services c7gn.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 architecture. The configuration supplies 16 dedicated physical cores running at 2.6 GHz with one execution thread per core, backed by 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core cluster. System memory totals 32.0 GB, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Network connectivity provides a 50 Gbps baseline throughput. There is no bundled local storage and no hardware GPU accelerators included.

Benchmark evaluations position the c7gn.4xlarge in the top 25 percent for memory subsystem metrics, highlighted by a strong PassMark memory score and uncached large-block write throughput of 96.92 GB/sec. General multi-core processing delivers middle-tier results, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 13275.0 and stress-ng multi-core throughput of 24498.72. Static web throughput reaches 29.56 GB/sec, while Redis SET performance registers at 26.87 million operations per second. PassMark CPU encryption tests and medium-scale LLM prompt processing exhibit weaker performance profiles compared to x86 equivalents lacking dedicated ARM cryptographic acceleration extensions.

The instance delivers architectural efficiency by pairing dedicated, non-hyperthreaded Neoverse-V1 cores with high-bandwidth 50 Gbps networking. Because all persistent storage must be attached via network volumes such as Amazon EBS, disk performance is decoupled from local drive failures but remains bounded by remote interface limits. The balanced compute density and high packet routing capabilities offer favorable resource utilization for network-heavy compute jobs without the overhead of unused local NVMe storage.

AWS c7gn.4xlarge is suited for network-intensive compute tasks, including network virtual appliances, firewalls, high-throughput web front ends, containerized microservices, distributed CI/CD compilation, and mid-scale data processing pipelines.
